uncertainObservations: The upper-viewer-left constellation is a clearly humanoid winged figure holding an open book. It is drawn as star-lines, not as a living person, so I did not include it in figureCount; if constellation humanoids count, figureCount would be 2. Flagging the ambiguity as the schema requires.
I did not attempt an exact count of the celestial wheel's radial spokes or of the glyphs on its inscribed bands; the subdivisions are too fine and repeat at several radii.
The number of floating planet orbs is not reliably countable: some are partly cut by the frame edge, some blend into the water reflections and some sit inside the wheel's field. Recorded as null.
The device on the platform at the figure's viewer-right reads as a graduated ring or small astrolabe/armillary on a pedestal, but I cannot resolve its type with confidence.
I cannot tell whether the raised fingertip makes contact with the wheel's rim or stops just short of it.
The shoreline structures at the left and right edges are small and partly cut by the frame; I counted two but a further structure hidden in the glare is possible.
The figure's sex and age are not determinable — the figure is seen entirely from behind.
Whether the horizon glow is sunset or sunrise cannot be determined.
